instruction:
## User Account

- Users sign up with email and password
- Users log in with email and password
- Users can change their password
- Users can delete their account (all their todos, including those in trash, are permanently deleted)

## User Profile

- Each user has a profile with: display name
- Users can edit their display name
- Users cannot view other users' profiles (this is a private todo app)

## Creating Todos

- Users can create a todo with:
  - Title (required)
  - Description (optional, can be left empty)
  - Start date (optional, can be left empty)
  - Due date (optional, can be left empty)
- Newly created todos are incomplete by default

## Edit History

- Each todo has an edit history
- Every time a todo is edited, a history entry is created
- Each history entry records:
  - When the edit was made
  - What the title was changed to (if changed)
  - What the description was changed to (if changed)
  - What the start date was changed to (if changed)
  - What the due date was changed to (if changed)

## Deleting Todos

- Users can delete their own todos
- Deleted todos are not permanently removed (soft delete)
- Deleted todos no longer appear in the normal todo list

## Trash

- Users can view a list of their deleted todos (trash)
- Users can restore a deleted todo from the trash (it returns to the normal todo list)
- Users can permanently delete a todo from the trash
- Permanently deleting a todo also deletes its edit history

## Privacy

- Each user's todos are completely private
- Users can only see their own todos
- There is no way to view, access, or share another user's todos

models.name: todo_app_guests
models.description:
Temporary guest accounts identified by device fingerprint for anonymous access.

Guest accounts allow unauthenticated users to access the application without registration. Each guest is identified by a unique device fingerprint generated from browser or device characteristics.

Guest accounts are temporary and do not have persistent credentials like email or password. They can create and manage todos during their session, but data is tied to the device fingerprint. Guests can later convert to member accounts by registering with email and password.

plainFields.name: device_fingerprint
plainFields.description:
Unique device identifier for guest account recognition.

Generated from browser or device characteristics to identify anonymous users. Used to associate guest sessions and guest-owned todos with the correct guest account. Must be unique across all guest accounts.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Record creation timestamp.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Record last update timestamp.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. Null means active.

models.name: todo_app_guest_sessions
models.description:
Temporary session tokens for guest access with short expiration.

Provides authenticated access for anonymous users identified by device fingerprint. Sessions are short-lived and automatically expire for security. Each session tracks the IP address and request metadata for audit purposes.

References {@link todo_app_guests} for the guest identity. Sessions are created during guest login and invalidated on logout or expiration.

foreignFields.name: todo_app_guest_id
foreignFields.description:
References the guest account that owns this session.

Links to {@link todo_app_guests} for the anonymous user identity. Multiple sessions can belong to the same guest (e.g., multiple devices or browsers).

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description:
IP address of the client that created this session.

Used for security audit and session validation. Captured at session creation time.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description:
URL path where the session was initiated.

Tracks the entry point for audit and analytics purposes.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description:
Referrer URL that led to session creation.

Tracks the traffic source for analytics. Can be empty if direct access.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when this session was created.

Used for session age calculation and audit trails.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when this session expires.

Guest sessions have short expiration times for security. After this time, the session is invalid and must be recreated.

models.name: todo_app_members
models.description:
Registered member accounts with email/password authentication credentials and profile data.

This table stores the core identity and authentication data for authenticated users. Each member can log in, manage their private todos, and access edit history features.

Authentication: Members authenticate using email and password_hash. The email field is unique and serves as the primary login identifier.

Profile: Each member has a display_name that identifies them within the application. This is the only profile attribute as the app is private and users cannot view other users' profiles.

Lifecycle: Members can delete their accounts, which triggers soft delete (deleted_at). Account deletion cascades to permanently delete all associated todos including those in trash, along with their edit histories.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description:
Email address used for authentication and account identification.

This field serves as the unique login identifier for member authentication. Members use this email along with their password to log in. The value must be unique across all members to ensure each account is distinct.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description:
Hashed password for authentication security.

Stores the bcrypt or similar hash of the member's password. Never store plain text passwords. This field is required for all members and is used during login verification.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description:
Member's display name shown in the application interface.

This is the user-facing name that identifies the member within the todo application. Members can edit this value through their profile settings. Unlike public applications, this display name is only visible to the member themselves as todos are completely private.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the member account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the member account was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the member account was soft deleted. Null for active accounts. When set, triggers cascade deletion of all member's todos and related data.

models.name: todo_app_member_sessions
models.description:
JWT session tokens for member authentication with access and refresh token support.

This table tracks all authenticated login sessions for {@link todo_app_members}. Each session record contains the access and refresh tokens required for API authentication, along with client information for security auditing.

Sessions are created during login and validated on each authenticated request. Expired sessions are automatically rejected by the auth middleware.

foreignFields.name: todo_app_member_id
foreignFields.description:
References the {@link todo_app_members} who owns this session.

Each session belongs to exactly one member. When a member logs in, a new session is created. Sessions are invalidated on logout or when they expire.

plainFields.name: access_token
plainFields.description:
JWT access token for API authentication.

This token is included in the Authorization header of API requests. It has a short expiration time (typically 15-30 minutes) for security.

plainFields.name: refresh_token
plainFields.description:
JWT refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.

This token has a longer expiration time and is used to request new access tokens without requiring the user to re-enter credentials. Stored securely and rotated on use.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description:
IP address of the client that created this session.

Recorded for security auditing and to detect suspicious login patterns. Used to identify the geographic location and device network.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description:
URL of the page where the login was initiated.

Captures the entry point for the authentication flow. Useful for redirecting users back after successful login and for analytics.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description:
HTTP referrer header from the login request.

Indicates which page or external site referred the user to the login page. Used for security analysis and traffic source tracking.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when this session was created.

Set automatically when the member successfully logs in. Used for session age calculations and audit trails.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when this session expires.

Sessions are automatically invalidated after this time. Members must log in again to create a new session. Typically set to 7-30 days from creation depending on security policy.

models.name: todo_app_member_password_resets
models.description:
Password reset tokens with expiration for member account recovery.

Stores temporary tokens generated when members request password resets. Each token is single-use and expires after a configured time period for security. Tokens are validated during the password change flow and invalidated after use or expiration.

References {@link todo_app_members} for the account requesting recovery. Multiple tokens can exist per member (e.g., if multiple reset requests are made), but only the most recent unexpired token should be valid.

foreignFields.name: todo_app_member_id
foreignFields.description:
Reference to the member account requesting password reset.

Establishes ownership of this reset token to a specific {@link todo_app_members} account. Multiple reset tokens can exist for the same member over time (e.g., if previous tokens expired unused). The token is validated against this member during password reset flow.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description:
Unique password reset token for lookup and validation.

Randomly generated secure string sent to the member's email. Used to authenticate the password reset request without requiring login. Must be unique across all reset tokens and is invalidated after use or expiration.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description:
Token expiration timestamp for security.

Defines when this reset token becomes invalid. Typically set to a short duration (e.g., 1 hour) from creation time to limit the window for unauthorized access. Tokens past this timestamp must be rejected during password reset validation.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description:
Token creation timestamp for audit and ordering.

Records when this password reset token was generated. Used for auditing reset requests and for selecting the most recent valid token when multiple exist for a member.

models.name: todo_app_member_email_verifications
models.description:
Email verification tokens for member registration confirmation.

Stores verification tokens sent to new members during the registration process. Each token is unique and expires after a configured time period. When a member clicks the verification link, the token is validated and the verified_at timestamp is recorded.

Related to {@link todo_app_members} via foreign key. Members can have multiple verification tokens over time (e.g., if they request new verification emails), but only one unexpired, unverified token should be active at any time.

foreignFields.name: todo_app_member_id
foreignFields.description:
References the member account this verification token belongs to.

Links to {@link todo_app_members}. Each verification record is associated with exactly one member. The token is created during registration and consumed when the member verifies their email address.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description:
Unique verification token sent to the member's email address.

Generated as a random secure string during registration. Used to validate the email verification link when the member clicks it. Must be unique across all verification records.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when this verification token expires.

Set at creation time based on system configuration (e.g., 24 hours). After this time, the token cannot be used for verification and a new token must be generated.

plainFields.name: verified_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when the member successfully verified their email.

Null until the member clicks the verification link and the token is validated. Once set, indicates the email has been confirmed and the member account is fully activated.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this verification token was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this verification token was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when this verification token was soft deleted.

Null while the record is active. Set when the verification record is soft deleted (e.g., after successful verification or cleanup of expired tokens).

models.name: todo_app_todos
models.description:
Main todo entity storing task information including title, description, optional dates, completion status, and soft-delete state.

Each todo belongs to exactly one {@link todo_app_members} and tracks the task's lifecycle from creation through completion or deletion. The title is required while description and date fields are optional.

Completion status (is_completed) defaults to false for new todos. Soft-delete is implemented via is_deleted and deleted_at fields, allowing todos to be moved to trash and potentially restored. Permanently deleted todos are removed from this table along with their {@link todo_app_todo_edit_histories}.

foreignFields.name: todo_app_member_id
foreignFields.description:
References the {@link todo_app_members} who owns this todo.

Every todo must belong to exactly one member. This foreign key establishes ownership and enables privacy isolation - members can only access their own todos.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description:
The todo's title or summary.

This is a required field that briefly describes what task needs to be completed. Must be provided when creating a new todo.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description:
Optional detailed description of the todo.

Can be left empty if no additional details are needed. Provides context or instructions for completing the task.

plainFields.name: start_date
plainFields.description:
Optional date when the todo should be started.

Can be left empty if no specific start date is needed. Used for planning and scheduling purposes.

plainFields.name: due_date
plainFields.description:
Optional date by which the todo should be completed.

Can be left empty if no deadline is set. Used for tracking upcoming tasks and priorities.

plainFields.name: is_completed
plainFields.description:
Completion status flag indicating whether the todo has been finished.

Defaults to false for newly created todos. When toggled to true, the todo is marked as complete but remains in the list unless deleted.

plainFields.name: is_deleted
plainFields.description:
Soft-delete flag indicating whether the todo has been moved to trash.

When true, the todo is hidden from the normal todo list but can be viewed in trash and potentially restored. Defaults to false.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when the todo was soft-deleted (moved to trash).

Null if the todo has never been deleted. Set when is_deleted becomes true, cleared if the todo is restored from trash.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the todo was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the todo was last updated.

models.name: todo_app_todo_edit_histories
models.description:
Edit history entries automatically created when todos are modified, recording what fields changed and when.

Each entry captures the state of changed fields at the time of edit, providing a complete audit trail of all modifications made to a {@link todo_app_todos} record. Entries are created automatically by the system whenever a todo is updated through the edit operation.

History entries are append-only and cannot be modified after creation. They are permanently deleted only when the associated todo is permanently deleted from the trash.

foreignFields.name: todo_app_todo_id
foreignFields.description:
Reference to the todo that was edited.

Establishes ownership relationship to {@link todo_app_todos}. Each history entry belongs to exactly one todo and tracks modifications made to that todo over time. When the parent todo is permanently deleted, all associated history entries are cascading deleted.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when the edit was made.

Records the exact point in time when the todo modification occurred. Used for ordering history entries chronologically and displaying edit timeline to users.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description:
New title value after the edit.

Stores the updated title if the title field was changed during this edit operation. Null if the title was not modified in this particular edit. Allows reconstruction of title change history by examining non-null values across entries.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description:
New description value after the edit.

Stores the updated description if the description field was changed during this edit operation. Null if the description was not modified. Supports optional description field on the parent todo.

plainFields.name: started_at
plainFields.description:
New start date value after the edit.

Stores the updated start date if the start date field was changed during this edit operation. Null if the start date was not modified or if it was set to null. Tracks changes to optional start date attribute.

plainFields.name: due_at
plainFields.description:
New due date value after the edit.

Stores the updated due date if the due date field was changed during this edit operation. Null if the due date was not modified or if it was set to null. Tracks changes to optional due date attribute.

### `todo_app_guests`

Temporary guest accounts identified by device fingerprint for anonymous
access.

Guest accounts allow unauthenticated users to access the application
without registration. Each guest is identified by a unique device
fingerprint generated from browser or device characteristics.

Guest accounts are temporary and do not have persistent credentials like
email or password. They can create and manage todos during their session,
but data is tied to the device fingerprint. Guests can later convert to
member accounts by registering with email and password.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `device_fingerprint`
  > Unique device identifier for guest account recognition.
  >
  > Generated from browser or device characteristics to identify anonymous
  > users. Used to associate guest sessions and guest-owned todos with the
  > correct guest account. Must be unique across all guest accounts.
- `created_at`: Record creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Record last update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp. Null means active.

### `todo_app_guest_sessions`

Temporary session tokens for guest access with short expiration.

Provides authenticated access for anonymous users identified by device
fingerprint. Sessions are short-lived and automatically expire for
security. Each session tracks the IP address and request metadata for
audit purposes.

References [todo_app_guests](#todo_app_guests) for the guest identity. Sessions are
created during guest login and invalidated on logout or expiration.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `todo_app_guest_id`
  > References the guest account that owns this session.
  >
  > Links to [todo_app_guests](#todo_app_guests) for the anonymous user identity.
  > Multiple sessions can belong to the same guest (e.g., multiple devices or
  > browsers).
- `ip`
  > IP address of the client that created this session.
  >
  > Used for security audit and session validation. Captured at session
  > creation time.
- `href`
  > URL path where the session was initiated.
  >
  > Tracks the entry point for audit and analytics purposes.
- `referrer`
  > Referrer URL that led to session creation.
  >
  > Tracks the traffic source for analytics. Can be empty if direct access.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when this session was created.
  >
  > Used for session age calculation and audit trails.
- `expired_at`
  > Timestamp when this session expires.
  >
  > Guest sessions have short expiration times for security. After this time,
  > the session is invalid and must be recreated.

and profile data.

This table stores the core identity and authentication data for
authenticated users. Each member can log in, manage their private todos,
and access edit history features.

Authentication: Members authenticate using email and password_hash. The
email field is unique and serves as the primary login identifier.

Profile: Each member has a display_name that identifies them within the
application. This is the only profile attribute as the app is private and
users cannot view other users' profiles.

Lifecycle: Members can delete their accounts, which triggers soft delete
(deleted_at). Account deletion cascades to permanently delete all
associated todos including those in trash, along with their edit
histories.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `email`
  > Email address used for authentication and account identification.
  >
  > This field serves as the unique login identifier for member
  > authentication. Members use this email along with their password to log
  > in. The value must be unique across all members to ensure each account is
  > distinct.
- `password_hash`
  > Hashed password for authentication security.
  >
  > Stores the bcrypt or similar hash of the member's password. Never store
  > plain text passwords. This field is required for all members and is used
  > during login verification.
- `display_name`
  > Member's display name shown in the application interface.
  >
  > This is the user-facing name that identifies the member within the todo
  > application. Members can edit this value through their profile settings.
  > Unlike public applications, this display name is only visible to the
  > member themselves as todos are completely private.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the member account was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the member account was last updated.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when the member account was soft deleted. Null for active
  > accounts. When set, triggers cascade deletion of all member's todos and
  > related data.

### `todo_app_member_sessions`

JWT session tokens for member authentication with access and refresh
token support.

This table tracks all authenticated login sessions for {@link
todo_app_members}. Each session record contains the access and refresh
tokens required for API authentication, along with client information for
security auditing.

Sessions are created during login and validated on each authenticated
request. Expired sessions are automatically rejected by the auth
middleware.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `todo_app_member_id`
  > References the [todo_app_members](#todo_app_members) who owns this session.
  >
  > Each session belongs to exactly one member. When a member logs in, a new
  > session is created. Sessions are invalidated on logout or when they
  > expire.
- `access_token`
  > JWT access token for API authentication.
  >
  > This token is included in the Authorization header of API requests. It
  > has a short expiration time (typically 15-30 minutes) for security.
- `refresh_token`
  > JWT refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.
  >
  > This token has a longer expiration time and is used to request new access
  > tokens without requiring the user to re-enter credentials. Stored
  > securely and rotated on use.
- `ip`
  > IP address of the client that created this session.
  >
  > Recorded for security auditing and to detect suspicious login patterns.
  > Used to identify the geographic location and device network.
- `href`
  > URL of the page where the login was initiated.
  >
  > Captures the entry point for the authentication flow. Useful for
  > redirecting users back after successful login and for analytics.
- `referrer`
  > HTTP referrer header from the login request.
  >
  > Indicates which page or external site referred the user to the login
  > page. Used for security analysis and traffic source tracking.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when this session was created.
  >
  > Set automatically when the member successfully logs in. Used for session
  > age calculations and audit trails.
- `expired_at`
  > Timestamp when this session expires.
  >
  > Sessions are automatically invalidated after this time. Members must log
  > in again to create a new session. Typically set to 7-30 days from
  > creation depending on security policy.

### `todo_app_member_password_resets`

Password reset tokens with expiration for member account recovery.

Stores temporary tokens generated when members request password resets.
Each token is single-use and expires after a configured time period for
security. Tokens are validated during the password change flow and
invalidated after use or expiration.

References [todo_app_members](#todo_app_members) for the account requesting recovery.
Multiple tokens can exist per member (e.g., if multiple reset requests
are made), but only the most recent unexpired token should be valid.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `todo_app_member_id`
  > Reference to the member account requesting password reset.
  >
  > Establishes ownership of this reset token to a specific {@link
  > todo_app_members} account. Multiple reset tokens can exist for the same
  > member over time (e.g., if previous tokens expired unused). The token is
  > validated against this member during password reset flow.
- `token`
  > Unique password reset token for lookup and validation.
  >
  > Randomly generated secure string sent to the member's email. Used to
  > authenticate the password reset request without requiring login. Must be
  > unique across all reset tokens and is invalidated after use or
  > expiration.
- `expires_at`
  > Token expiration timestamp for security.
  >
  > Defines when this reset token becomes invalid. Typically set to a short
  > duration (e.g., 1 hour) from creation time to limit the window for
  > unauthorized access. Tokens past this timestamp must be rejected during
  > password reset validation.
- `created_at`
  > Token creation timestamp for audit and ordering.
  >
  > Records when this password reset token was generated. Used for auditing
  > reset requests and for selecting the most recent valid token when
  > multiple exist for a member.

### `todo_app_member_email_verifications`

Email verification tokens for member registration confirmation.

Stores verification tokens sent to new members during the registration
process. Each token is unique and expires after a configured time period.
When a member clicks the verification link, the token is validated and
the verified_at timestamp is recorded.

Related to [todo_app_members](#todo_app_members) via foreign key. Members can have
multiple verification tokens over time (e.g., if they request new
verification emails), but only one unexpired, unverified token should be
active at any time.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `todo_app_member_id`
  > References the member account this verification token belongs to.
  >
  > Links to [todo_app_members](#todo_app_members). Each verification record is associated
  > with exactly one member. The token is created during registration and
  > consumed when the member verifies their email address.
- `token`
  > Unique verification token sent to the member's email address.
  >
  > Generated as a random secure string during registration. Used to validate
  > the email verification link when the member clicks it. Must be unique
  > across all verification records.
- `expires_at`
  > Timestamp when this verification token expires.
  >
  > Set at creation time based on system configuration (e.g., 24 hours).
  > After this time, the token cannot be used for verification and a new
  > token must be generated.
- `verified_at`
  > Timestamp when the member successfully verified their email.
  >
  > Null until the member clicks the verification link and the token is
  > validated. Once set, indicates the email has been confirmed and the
  > member account is fully activated.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this verification token was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when this verification token was last updated.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when this verification token was soft deleted.
  >
  > Null while the record is active. Set when the verification record is soft
  > deleted (e.g., after successful verification or cleanup of expired
  > tokens).

### `todo_app_todos`

Main todo entity storing task information including title, description,
optional dates, completion status, and soft-delete state.

Each todo belongs to exactly one [todo_app_members](#todo_app_members) and tracks the
task's lifecycle from creation through completion or deletion. The title
is required while description and date fields are optional.

Completion status (is_completed) defaults to false for new todos.
Soft-delete is implemented via is_deleted and deleted_at fields, allowing
todos to be moved to trash and potentially restored. Permanently deleted
todos are removed from this table along with their {@link
todo_app_todo_edit_histories}.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `todo_app_member_id`
  > References the [todo_app_members](#todo_app_members) who owns this todo.
  >
  > Every todo must belong to exactly one member. This foreign key
  > establishes ownership and enables privacy isolation - members can only
  > access their own todos.
- `title`
  > The todo's title or summary.
  >
  > This is a required field that briefly describes what task needs to be
  > completed. Must be provided when creating a new todo.
- `description`
  > Optional detailed description of the todo.
  >
  > Can be left empty if no additional details are needed. Provides context
  > or instructions for completing the task.
- `start_date`
  > Optional date when the todo should be started.
  >
  > Can be left empty if no specific start date is needed. Used for planning
  > and scheduling purposes.
- `due_date`
  > Optional date by which the todo should be completed.
  >
  > Can be left empty if no deadline is set. Used for tracking upcoming tasks
  > and priorities.
- `is_completed`
  > Completion status flag indicating whether the todo has been finished.
  >
  > Defaults to false for newly created todos. When toggled to true, the todo
  > is marked as complete but remains in the list unless deleted.
- `is_deleted`
  > Soft-delete flag indicating whether the todo has been moved to trash.
  >
  > When true, the todo is hidden from the normal todo list but can be viewed
  > in trash and potentially restored. Defaults to false.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when the todo was soft-deleted (moved to trash).
  >
  > Null if the todo has never been deleted. Set when is_deleted becomes
  > true, cleared if the todo is restored from trash.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the todo was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the todo was last updated.

### `todo_app_todo_edit_histories`

Edit history entries automatically created when todos are modified,
recording what fields changed and when.

Each entry captures the state of changed fields at the time of edit,
providing a complete audit trail of all modifications made to a {@link
todo_app_todos} record. Entries are created automatically by the system
whenever a todo is updated through the edit operation.

History entries are append-only and cannot be modified after creation.
They are permanently deleted only when the associated todo is permanently
deleted from the trash.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `todo_app_todo_id`
  > Reference to the todo that was edited.
  >
  > Establishes ownership relationship to [todo_app_todos](#todo_app_todos). Each
  > history entry belongs to exactly one todo and tracks modifications made
  > to that todo over time. When the parent todo is permanently deleted, all
  > associated history entries are cascading deleted.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when the edit was made.
  >
  > Records the exact point in time when the todo modification occurred. Used
  > for ordering history entries chronologically and displaying edit timeline
  > to users.
- `title`
  > New title value after the edit.
  >
  > Stores the updated title if the title field was changed during this edit
  > operation. Null if the title was not modified in this particular edit.
  > Allows reconstruction of title change history by examining non-null
  > values across entries.
- `description`
  > New description value after the edit.
  >
  > Stores the updated description if the description field was changed
  > during this edit operation. Null if the description was not modified.
  > Supports optional description field on the parent todo.
- `started_at`
  > New start date value after the edit.
  >
  > Stores the updated start date if the start date field was changed during
  > this edit operation. Null if the start date was not modified or if it was
  > set to null. Tracks changes to optional start date attribute.
- `due_at`
  > New due date value after the edit.
  >
  > Stores the updated due date if the due date field was changed during this
  > edit operation. Null if the due date was not modified or if it was set to
  > null. Tracks changes to optional due date attribute.

instruction:
## User Account

- Users sign up with email and password
- Users log in with email and password
- Users can change their password
- Users can delete their account (all their todos, including those in trash, are permanently deleted)

## User Profile

- Each user has a profile with: display name
- Users can edit their display name
- Users cannot view other users' profiles (this is a private todo app)

## Creating Todos

- Users can create a todo with:
  - Title (required)
  - Description (optional, can be left empty)
  - Start date (optional, can be left empty)
  - Due date (optional, can be left empty)
- Newly created todos are incomplete by default

## Viewing Todos

- Users can view a list of their own todos
- The list is paginated
- Each todo in the list shows: title, completion status, start date (if set), due date (if set), and creation date
- Users can view a single todo to see all its details including full description

## Completing Todos

- Users can mark a todo as complete
- Users can mark a todo as incomplete
- This is a simple toggle between two states

## Editing Todos

- Users can edit their todo's title, description, start date, and due date
- Every edit is recorded in the todo's history

## Edit History

- Each todo has an edit history
- Every time a todo is edited, a history entry is created
- Each history entry records:
  - When the edit was made
  - What the title was changed to (if changed)
  - What the description was changed to (if changed)
  - What the start date was changed to (if changed)
  - What the due date was changed to (if changed)
- Users can view the full edit history of any of their todos
- History entries are sorted from most recent to oldest

## Deleting Todos

- Users can delete their own todos
- Deleted todos are not permanently removed (soft delete)
- Deleted todos no longer appear in the normal todo list

## Trash

- Users can view a list of their deleted todos (trash)
- The trash list is paginated
- Users can restore a deleted todo from the trash (it returns to the normal todo list)
- Users can permanently delete a todo from the trash
- Permanently deleting a todo also deletes its edit history

## Filtering Todos

- Users can filter their todo list by completion status:
  - All todos
  - Only complete todos
  - Only incomplete todos

## Sorting Todos

- Users can sort their todo list by:
  - Creation date (newest first or oldest first)
  - Start date (earliest first or latest first)
  - Due date (earliest first or latest first)
- Todos without a start date appear at the end when sorting by start date
- Todos without a due date appear at the end when sorting by due date

## Privacy

- Each user's todos are completely private
- Users can only see their own todos
- There is no way to view, access, or share another user's todos

operations.description:
Register a new guest account using device fingerprint for anonymous access.

Creates a guest account identified by the unique device fingerprint. The system generates JWT access and refresh tokens for authenticated guest sessions. Access tokens are short-lived for security, while refresh tokens allow obtaining new access tokens without re-registration.

The device fingerprint must be unique across all guest accounts. If a guest account already exists for the provided fingerprint, the operation may return existing tokens or create a new session depending on implementation policy.

Session metadata including IP address, page URL, and referrer are captured for audit and security purposes. Guest sessions have automatic expiration times for security.

operations.name: join

Generate new access token and optionally new refresh token. Update session expired_at timestamp. Return new token pair in IAuthorized response. Invalidate old refresh token if rotating. Handle expired/invalid tokens with 401 error.
operations.description:
Refresh guest authentication tokens using a valid refresh token.

Exchanges a valid refresh token for a new access token and refresh token pair. This operation allows guests to maintain authenticated sessions without re-registering with their device fingerprint.

The refresh token must be valid, unexpired, and match an existing session in the database. Invalid or expired tokens result in authentication failure. The operation updates the session expiration timestamp to extend the guest's access period.

Token rotation may be implemented for enhanced security, where each refresh invalidates the previous refresh token and issues a new one.

responseBody.description: New JWT tokens for continued guest session.

Register a new member account with email, password, and display name.

This operation creates a new authenticated user account in the todo_app_members table. The email serves as the unique login identifier and must not already exist in the system. The password is securely hashed before storage. The display name is the user-facing identifier within the application.

Upon successful registration, the system generates a JWT access token and refresh token, stores them in todo_app_member_sessions with client information (IP address, page href, referrer) for security auditing, and returns both tokens in the response. The member can immediately use the access token for authenticated API requests.

Email validation ensures proper format. Password must meet security requirements (minimum length, complexity). Duplicate email addresses return a 409 conflict error. All timestamps (created_at, updated_at) are set automatically.

Authenticate a member with email and password to obtain JWT tokens.

This operation validates member credentials against the todo_app_members table. The email is looked up and the provided password is compared against the stored password_hash using secure bcrypt verification. The account must be active (deleted_at is null) to successfully authenticate.

Upon successful authentication, the system generates a new JWT access token (short-lived, typically 15-30 minutes) and refresh token (longer-lived, typically 7-30 days), creates a session record in todo_app_member_sessions with client information (IP address, page href, referrer) for security auditing, and returns both tokens in the response.

Invalid email or password returns 401 unauthorized. Accounts that have been soft deleted (deleted_at is set) return 403 forbidden. The access token is used in the Authorization header for subsequent API requests.

Upon successful validation, the system generates a new JWT access token and refresh token pair, updates the session record in todo_app_member_sessions with the new tokens, and returns them in the response. This enables continuous authenticated sessions without requiring repeated login.

Invalid or expired refresh tokens return 401 unauthorized. Members whose accounts have been soft deleted return 403 forbidden. The refresh token flow maintains session continuity while enforcing security through token expiration.

operations.description:

This endpoint returns todos filtered by completion status and sorted according to the specified criteria. The filter options include all todos, only complete todos, or only incomplete todos. Sorting can be applied by creation date, start date, or due date with configurable direction.

When sorting by start date or due date, todos without the respective date are placed at the end of the list regardless of sort direction. The response includes pagination metadata for navigating large result sets.

Query the todo_app_todos table for todos owned by the authenticated member.

- 'all' or undefined: return all todos (both complete and incomplete)
- 'complete': return only todos where completed = true
- 'incomplete': return only todos where completed = false

Apply sorting based on the requested sort field and direction:
- creation_date: sort by created_at column
- start_date: sort by started_at column, nulls at end
- due_date: sort by due_at column, nulls at end

For start_date and due_date sorting, use COALESCE or similar to place null values at the end regardless of ASC/DESC direction.

Apply pagination using cursor-based or offset-based pagination.

2. Validate title is provided and not empty

4. Set is_deleted to false (default)
5. Set created_at and updated_at to current timestamp

- Optional fields (description, start_date, due_date) can be null

operations.description:
Update an existing todo's editable fields including title, description, start date, and due date.

This operation allows members to modify their todo's content and scheduling information. The title is required while description, start date, and due date are optional - only provided fields are updated, leaving others unchanged.

Upon successful update, the system automatically creates a new entry in the todo's edit history, recording what fields were changed and their new values. This history entry is created without any additional action from the user.

The response returns the complete updated todo entity with all fields including system-managed fields like completion status and timestamps. Users can only update their own todos - attempts to access another user's todo will be denied.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Update the todo identified by todoId with the provided fields.

1. Verify authentication: ensure the request is from an authenticated member
2. Find the todo by todoId and verify ownership (todo_app_member_id matches authenticated user)
3. If todo not found or not owned by user, return 404 or 403 error
4. Update only the fields provided in the request body (title, description, start_date, due_date)
5. Update the updated_at timestamp to current time
6. Automatically create a todo_edit_histories entry recording:
   - The timestamp of the edit
   - Which fields were changed and their new values
7. Return the complete updated todo entity

Edge cases:
- If todoId does not exist, return 404
- If todo belongs to another user, return 403
- If title is provided but empty, return validation error
- Preserve null values for optional fields when not provided

operations.description:
Move a todo to trash by marking it as deleted.

This operation soft-deletes a todo by setting its is_deleted flag to true and recording the deletion timestamp. The todo is hidden from the normal todo list but remains accessible in the trash where it can be restored or permanently deleted.

The deleted todo's edit history is preserved, allowing users to restore the todo with its complete history intact. Only the todo owner can delete their own todos due to privacy isolation.

This operation implements soft deletion - the todo is not permanently removed from the database and can be recovered from trash if needed.
operations.name: erase

Soft-delete a todo by updating is_deleted to true and setting deleted_at to current timestamp.

1. Verify the todo exists and belongs to the authenticated member (privacy isolation)
2. Verify the todo is not already deleted (is_deleted = false)
3. Update is_deleted = true and deleted_at = current timestamp
4. Return success (null response body)

Edge cases:
- Todo not found: return 404
- Todo belongs to another user: return 403 (should not happen with proper authorization)
- Todo already deleted: return 400 or 409 conflict

The todo_app_member_id is obtained from the authenticated session context, not from the request body.

operations.description:
Retrieve paginated edit history entries for a specific todo.

This endpoint returns all edit history entries associated with the specified todo, allowing users to review the complete evolution of their todo from creation through all edits. Each history entry captures what fields were changed and when the edit was made.

Edit history entries are automatically created by the system whenever a todo is edited. Users can only view edit history for todos they own. Entries are sorted in descending order by timestamp (most recent first) by default.

The operation supports pagination to handle large edit histories efficiently. Users can filter by date ranges and sort by creation timestamp.

operations.specification: Query todo_app_todo_edit_histories table filtered by todo_app_todo_id matching the path parameter. Verify the todo exists and belongs to the authenticated user before returning history entries. Apply pagination with cursor-based or offset-based approach. Default sort order is created_at DESC (most recent first). Support optional date range filtering on created_at. Return ITodoAppTodoEditHistory.ISummary for each entry containing id, created_at, and changed field values (title, description, started_at, due_at). Handle edge case where todo has no edit history (return empty array). Ensure cascade delete relationship is respected - if todo is permanently deleted, history entries no longer exist.

operations.description:
Retrieves a single edit history entry for a specific todo.

This operation returns the complete details of one edit history entry, including the timestamp when the edit was made and all field values that were captured during that edit operation. Each history entry shows what the title, description, start date, and due date were changed to (if those fields were modified in that particular edit).

Edit history entries are automatically created by the system whenever a user edits their todo. Users can only access edit history for todos they own, ensuring complete privacy isolation between users.

The history entry includes optional fields for title, description, started_at, and due_at - each field is non-null only if that specific field was changed during the edit operation.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the todo_app_todo_edit_histories table by primary key (historyId) with ownership validation.

1. Verify the todo identified by todoId exists and belongs to the authenticated member
2. Query todo_app_todo_edit_histories WHERE id = historyId AND todo_app_todo_id = todoId
3. Return 404 if no matching history entry found (or if todo ownership doesn't match)
4. Return the full history entry record with all captured field values

The todoId parameter ensures the history entry belongs to the correct parent todo. This provides an additional security layer beyond just the historyId.

Edge cases:
- Return 404 if todoId doesn't exist or doesn't belong to the authenticated user
- Return 404 if historyId doesn't exist or doesn't match the todoId
- Include all optional fields (title, description, started_at, due_at) even if null

ITodoAppMember.IAuthorized.description:
Authentication response containing member identification and JWT tokens after successful login, registration, or token refresh.

This DTO is returned by the /todoApp/auth/member/join, /todoApp/auth/member/login, and /todoApp/auth/member/refresh operations. Request body for refreshing guest authentication tokens.

Contains the refresh token to exchange for new credentials and session context information for audit purposes. The refresh token must be valid and unexpired.

filter.description:
Filter todos by completion status.

Controls which todos are included in the result set based on their completion state. The 'all' option returns both complete and incomplete todos. The 'complete' option returns only todos marked as finished. The 'incomplete' option returns only todos that are still pending.

When not provided or null, defaults to 'all' showing all todos regardless of completion status.

sort.description:

Determines which attribute is used to sort the results. The 'creation_date' option orders by when todos were created. The 'start_date' option orders by the planned start date. The 'due_date' option orders by the deadline.

When not provided or null, defaults to 'creation_date'. When sorting by start_date or due_date, todos without the respective date appear at the end of the list regardless of sort direction.

sortDirection.description:
Sort direction for ordering the todo list.

Controls whether results are ordered in ascending or descending order. 'ASC' returns results from oldest/earliest to newest/latest. 'DESC' returns results from newest/latest to oldest/earliest.

When not provided or null, defaults to 'DESC' for creation_date sorting (newest first) and 'ASC' for start_date and due_date sorting (earliest first).

Specifies which page of results to retrieve. Page numbering starts from 1, so the first page is page 1 (not 0). This enables navigation through large result sets by requesting one page at a time.

When not provided, defaults to page 1. Must be at least 1 - values less than 1 are invalid.

Maximum number of records per page.

Controls how many todo items are returned in a single response. This enables clients to manage response size and implement efficient pagination. The actual number of records returned may be less than this value on the final page or when total records are fewer than the limit.

When not provided, defaults to 20. Must be between 1 and 100 inclusive - values outside this range are invalid.

ITodoAppTodo.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for retrieving a filtered and sorted list of todos with pagination support.

This DTO defines the query criteria for listing todos owned by the authenticated member. The filter parameter controls which todos are returned based on completion status. The sort parameter determines the ordering field, while sortDirection controls ascending or descending order. Pagination is handled through page and limit parameters.

The filter supports three modes: 'all' returns both complete and incomplete todos, 'complete' returns only finished todos, and 'incomplete' returns only pending todos. When sorting by start_date or due_date, todos without the respective date appear at the end of the list regardless of sort direction.

ITodoAppTodo.description:
Complete todo entity representing a task with all its attributes and relations.

This is the main response type for todo operations, containing the full todo record including title, optional description and dates, completion and deletion status, audit timestamps, the owning member, and all edit history entries.

The {@link member} property provides the todo owner's summary information via BELONGS-TO relation. The {@link editHistories} array contains all historical edits made to this todo as a HAS-MANY composition. Nullable fields ({@link description}, {@link startDate}, {@link dueDate}, {@link deletedAt}) use oneOf to represent null values when not set.

Sort field enumeration for ordering todo list results.

This enum defines the available fields for sorting todo lists. The 'creation_date' option orders todos by when they were created. The 'start_date' option orders by the planned start date, with todos lacking a start date appearing at the end. The 'due_date' option orders by the deadline, with todos lacking a due date appearing at the end.

This type is used in conjunction with {@link IESortDirection} to control the complete sort behavior of todo list queries.

IESortDirection.description:
Sort direction enumeration for controlling the order of paginated list results.

This type defines the two possible sort directions: 'ASC' for ascending order (oldest to newest, earliest to latest) and 'DESC' for descending order (newest to oldest, latest to earliest). Used in list request parameters to specify how results should be ordered.

When used in nullable contexts, the default value is determined by the specific endpoint and sort field. For example, creation date sorting typically defaults to DESC (newest first), while start date and due date sorting typically default to ASC (earliest first).

Used in list request DTOs to control ORDER BY direction. When nullable in request DTOs, null defaults to endpoint-specific default (e.g., DESC for creation_date, ASC for date fields).

IETodoAppTodoFilter.description:
Filter options for retrieving todos based on completion status.

This enum defines three filtering modes for todo list queries. The 'all' option returns both complete and incomplete todos without any completion status filter. The 'complete' option returns only todos that have been marked as finished. The 'incomplete' option returns only todos that are still pending and not yet completed.

When 'all' is selected or when the filter parameter is null/undefined, the query returns all todos regardless of their completion state. This is useful for viewing the complete todo list. The 'complete' and 'incomplete' filters enable focused views on finished or pending tasks respectively.

text: Now I'll execute the Test agent to generate comprehensive E2E test suites. I'll pass all the testing-relevant requirements from your specifications.

instruction:
## User Account

- Users sign up with email and password
- Users log in with email and password
- Users can change their password
- Users can delete their account (all their todos, including those in trash, are permanently deleted)

## User Profile

- Each user has a profile with: display name
- Users can edit their display name
- Users cannot view other users' profiles (this is a private todo app)

## Creating Todos

- Users can create a todo with:
  - Title (required)
  - Description (optional, can be left empty)
  - Start date (optional, can be left empty)
  - Due date (optional, can be left empty)
- Newly created todos are incomplete by default

## Viewing Todos

- Users can view a list of their own todos
- The list is paginated
- Each todo in the list shows: title, completion status, start date (if set), due date (if set), and creation date
- Users can view a single todo to see all its details including full description

## Completing Todos

- Users can mark a todo as complete
- Users can mark a todo as incomplete
- This is a simple toggle between two states

## Editing Todos

- Users can edit their todo's title, description, start date, and due date
- Every edit is recorded in the todo's history

## Edit History

- Each todo has an edit history
- Every time a todo is edited, a history entry is created
- Each history entry records:
  - When the edit was made
  - What the title was changed to (if changed)
  - What the description was changed to (if changed)
  - What the start date was changed to (if changed)
  - What the due date was changed to (if changed)
- Users can view the full edit history of any of their todos
- History entries are sorted from most recent to oldest

## Deleting Todos

- Users can delete their own todos
- Deleted todos are not permanently removed (soft delete)
- Deleted todos no longer appear in the normal todo list

## Trash

- Users can view a list of their deleted todos (trash)
- The trash list is paginated
- Users can restore a deleted todo from the trash (it returns to the normal todo list)
- Users can permanently delete a todo from the trash
- Permanently deleting a todo also deletes its edit history

## Filtering Todos

- Users can filter their todo list by completion status:
  - All todos
  - Only complete todos
  - Only incomplete todos

## Sorting Todos

- Users can sort their todo list by:
  - Creation date (newest first or oldest first)
  - Start date (earliest first or latest first)
  - Due date (earliest first or latest first)
- Todos without a start date appear at the end when sorting by start date
- Todos without a due date appear at the end when sorting by due date

## Privacy

- Each user's todos are completely private
- Users can only see their own todos
- There is no way to view, access, or share another user's todos

scenario.draft: Test successful guest account registration with a unique device fingerprint. The guest provides a unique device fingerprint along with session context (href, referrer, and IP address). The system creates a new guest account with a generated UUID, generates JWT access and refresh tokens, and creates a guest session record with the provided metadata. Verify the response contains the guest ID, valid access token, refresh token, and expiration timestamps. Verify the access token is short-lived (e.g., 1 hour) and the refresh token has a longer lifetime (e.g., 7 days). Verify the session metadata (IP, href, referrer) is captured for audit purposes. This represents the primary success path for anonymous user onboarding.

dependencies.purpose:
Essential authentication prerequisite:
This join operation (post /todoApp/auth/guest/join) must be executed before any operations requiring 'guest' actor authorization.
It establishes the necessary user account and authentication context for the 'guest' actor, enabling subsequent API calls that depend on this specific authorization level.
Without this join operation, the main scenario endpoint and its dependencies will fail due to insufficient authentication credentials.

First, register a guest with a specific device fingerprint to establish an existing account. Then attempt to register again with the same device fingerprint. The system should handle this duplicate fingerprint scenario by returning the existing guest's tokens or creating a new session for the existing guest account. Verify the response contains valid authentication tokens and the guest ID matches the existing account. Verify no duplicate guest account is created. This tests the business logic for handling returning anonymous users who use the same device.

instruction:
## User Account

- Users sign up with email and password
- Users log in with email and password
- Users can change their password
- Users can delete their account (all their todos, including those in trash, are permanently deleted)

## User Profile

- Each user has a profile with: display name
- Users can edit their display name
- Users cannot view other users' profiles (this is a private todo app)

## Creating Todos

- Users can create a todo with:
  - Title (required)
  - Description (optional, can be left empty)
  - Start date (optional, can be left empty)
  - Due date (optional, can be left empty)
- Newly created todos are incomplete by default

## Viewing Todos

- Users can view a list of their own todos
- The list is paginated
- Each todo in the list shows: title, completion status, start date (if set), due date (if set), and creation date
- Users can view a single todo to see all its details including full description

## Completing Todos

- Users can mark a todo as complete
- Users can mark a todo as incomplete
- This is a simple toggle between two states

## Editing Todos

- Users can edit their todo's title, description, start date, and due date
- Every edit is recorded in the todo's history

## Edit History

- Each todo has an edit history
- Every time a todo is edited, a history entry is created
- Each history entry records:
  - When the edit was made
  - What the title was changed to (if changed)
  - What the description was changed to (if changed)
  - What the start date was changed to (if changed)
  - What the due date was changed to (if changed)
- Users can view the full edit history of any of their todos
- History entries are sorted from most recent to oldest

## Deleting Todos

- Users can delete their own todos
- Deleted todos are not permanently removed (soft delete)
- Deleted todos no longer appear in the normal todo list

## Trash

- Users can view a list of their deleted todos (trash)
- The trash list is paginated
- Users can restore a deleted todo from the trash (it returns to the normal todo list)
- Users can permanently delete a todo from the trash
- Permanently deleting a todo also deletes its edit history

## Filtering Todos

- Users can filter their todo list by completion status:
  - All todos
  - Only complete todos
  - Only incomplete todos

## Sorting Todos

- Users can sort their todo list by:
  - Creation date (newest first or oldest first)
  - Start date (earliest first or latest first)
  - Due date (earliest first or latest first)
- Todos without a start date appear at the end when sorting by start date
- Todos without a due date appear at the end when sorting by due date

## Privacy

- Each user's todos are completely private
- Users can only see their own todos
- There is no way to view, access, or share another user's todos
